title: SparkBridge partner outbound micro-notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for SparkBridge outreach. Keep this lean — capture signals, hypothesis, and 1st-touch language. Not a polished playbook; meant for rapid iteration and sharing with Maya/Samir before we push to sequences.

Account snapshot (quick):
- Company: SparkBridge (mid-market fintech, payments orchestration + fraud insights)
- HQ: Denver (remote-heavy), ~220 headcount, Series B (2023)
- Recent headlines: raised growth round 2024, launched 'SmartRouting' product for multi-rail settlements, partnership with 2 regional acquirers.
- Why they matter: mid-size merchants; latent need to do semantic routing for dispute/resolution and automated customer replies — potential for embeddings/chat features.

Why Redwood could be interesting to them (hypothesis):
- Fit: They run high-volume synchronous flows (transaction status messages, dispute triage chatbots) where latency and cost matter. Redwood Dedicated or Private could provide predictable latency and data isolation for regulated workflows.
- Differentiator vs. hyperscalers: Lower per-token cost at scale + batching/caching features that align with repeating conversational patterns. Also our rollout/fallback policies matter for resilience during peak billing cycles.
- Risk: They may already have partial self-hosted LLM stack or be using large infra credits with cloud vendor. Need to probe infra/ops constraints.

Key personas to target (mapped to pain):
- Head of Platform / VP Eng (Kate R.) — cares about SLA, infra cost predictability, security primitives (KMS, VPC).
- Head of Product / Director of CX Automation (Ravi M.) — cares about reply quality, control over prompt updates, A/B testing rollouts for prompts, monitoring.
- Finance / Procurement (Proc lead) — pricing model, committed capacity vs usage, TCO comparables.

Signals to look for in public/linkedIn/Jira that increase priority:
- Job postings for ML infra, reliability, or embeddings engineer (indicates investment).
- Product release notes referencing "chatbot" "automated dispute response" "semantic matching".
- API rate limits / slowdowns threads on their community / engineering blog.

Outbound hypothesis + 1st-touch (email + optional LinkedIn):
Subject ideas: "Reduce per-message cost for SmartRouting replies" / "Quick note on lowering latency for dispute triage"
Body sketch (short):
- 1 line: noticed SparkBridge's SmartRouting -> congrats.
- 1 line: We help teams run production LLM features with predictable latency & cost (hosted -> dedicated -> private choices).
- 1 line: Specific ask: would you be open to a 20 min sync to see a quick model-to-cost comparison on a subset of your dispute triage prompts? I can show a ~30% token cost reduction for similar quality in a demo.
- CTA: 2 times next week + request for who owns the product/infra side.

Variation for Product persona (short LinkedIn):
- Quick note: built an eval set for dispute triage prompts for a payments client — help cut inference spend, keep quality. Would love to share anonymized results w/ your team.

Demo hooks / assets to prepare (low-effort, high-impact):
- 6–8 prompt examples that mirror dispute triage flows (we can adapt from public docs + typical patterns).
- A short benchmark showing latency & per-token $ across: hosted API (standard), dedicated (fixed throughput), and a private deployment (VPC), with traffic profile similar to SparkBridge (bursty morning settlement window).
- A one-slide TCO sketch comparing annualized spend vs. self-hosted LLM infra.

Objection handling (anticipated):
- "We already have a cloud credits deal / committed instance": acknowledge, then push value-add: "we can sit on top as a routing/fallback layer or run a private deployment that integrates with your KMS — think of it as a drop-in inference control plane, not a rip-and-replace."
- "Quality regression concerns": offer an eval run on a holdout prompt set + rollback policy + canary rollouts. Mention Redwood Optimize (quality monitoring + regressions alerts) as a guardrail.
- "Security/compliance": point to VPC private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. Offer SOC2 or compliance brief.
- "Too early / no headcount": suggest a pilot with our solutions engineering + a small set of prompts (2–4) to show tangible savings and ops signal within 2–3 weeks.

Metrics to capture if we get an intro/demo: (for later SRE/CS handoff)
- Avg tokens per session (current)
- Sessions per day & peak QPS windows
- Current latency p50/p95 for reply generation
- Current monthly inference spend + committed infra (if any)
- Security constraints (must-data-reside-on-prem? encryption-at-rest-only?)

Meeting prep checklist (for Jordan/Maya):
- [ ] Build a 10-min demo trace using 3 dispute triage prompts (annotate where prefix caching and batching help).
- [ ] Prepare cost curve slide (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with sample numbers for 100k/day sessions.
- [ ] Draft short eval agreement (2–4 week pilot, limited prompts, success metrics: token cost reduction >= 20% or parity + latency SLO met).
- [ ] Put a quick Slack thread in #bd-sparkbridge outlining outreach cadence and assign next steps.

Short-term outreach plan (first 14 days):
- Day 0: Send 1st-touch email to Head of Platform (Kate) + copy to Head of Product if publicly listed.
- Day 3: LinkedIn InMail to Product lead with eval hook + 1-pager.
- Day 7: Follow-up email with a small, anonymized case study (payments client) showing 25–35% cost reduction.
- Day 11: Final warm follow-up, offer specific times and a 'skip-the-call' one-pager if they'd rather pass to procurement.

Notes / open questions (things to research before outreach):
- Which cloud provider(s) do they primarily run on? (AWS/GCP/Azure) — affects private deployment feasibility and latency expectations.
- Are they using a vendor for fraud/chargeback automation (e.g., ChargebackOps) that might already own the conversation flow?
- Any recent incidents/public outages tied to customer-facing chatbots?
- Who is their legal/compliance owner for vendor reviews?

Random thoughts (brain dump):
- Could experiment with a "cost-first" subject line versus "quality-first" to see which resonates.
- If they are security-first, lead with Dedicated + Private options, push our audit logs and KMS story early.
- Consider offering to co-run a quick A/B on 1–2 merchants (anonymized) to show real-world impact on dispute resolution time — this could be a strong CS/metrics win.

Next actions (assignable):
- Jordan: draft initial email copy and put in GDrive under BD templates (target end of day).
- Maya: pull any existing payment-industry case studies we can anonymize for SparkBridge outreach.
- Samir: quick infra check — see if we have any prior infra runs on similar traffic patterns (100–200 QPS bursts).

Last line: keep it short and iterative. We want to learn if they care about inference economics (cost + latency) not just model choice. If they do, we have a credible path (pilot -> dedicated -> private) that maps directly to their scaling needs.

-- Jordan
